subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should OpenAI-compatible memory embedding fetches inherit `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, including exact-host trust when omitted and fail-closed behavior when explicitly false?
rationale: The code path is technically coherent and proven, but the permanent SSRF trust boundary for memory embeddings is a maintainer/security policy choice rather than an automation-safe repair.

options.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
options.body: Land this PR after a fresh mergeability/CI refresh, keeping provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` as the single trust surface for configured memory embedding endpoints.

options.title: Require a narrower policy before merge
options.body: Ask the contributor to adjust runtime, docs, and tests if maintainers want different omitted or explicit-false semantics for memory embeddings.

options.title: Reject this trust surface
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers want a separate memory-specific policy or no direct private-network memory embedding support.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
recommendation.body: Land this PR after a fresh mergeability/CI refresh, keeping provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` as the single trust surface for configured memory embedding endpoints.

likelyOwner.reason: Kaspre authored the merged exact-origin/custom provider SSRF contract that this PR extends, so they are the strongest history-backed owner for the security-boundary choice.
